uncited: - Parent Gaussian $G_a$ with mean $\mu_a$ and covariance $\Sigma_a$.
- Normal map $N_V^{(a)}$ corresponding to the reference view.
- A randomly sampled candidate position $\mu_b^c$ within the elliptical scale of $G_a$.
**Project Parent:** Project the parent Gaussian $G_a$ to the reference view $V^{(a)}$ to obtain the 2D pixel coordinate $\bar{x}_a$.
**Project Candidate:** Project the randomly sampled candidate position $\mu_b^c$ to the reference view $V^{(a)}$ to obtain the 2D pixel coordinate $\bar{x}_c$.
**Retrieve Normal:** Retrieve the surface normal vector $N_V^{(a)}(\bar{x}_a)$ from the normal map at pixel $\bar{x}_a$.
**Retrieve Gradient:** Retrieve the image gradient magnitude $\nabla I_V^{(a)}(\bar{x}_c)$ from the reference image at pixel $\bar{x}_c$.
**Compute Tangent Projection:** Calculate the perpendicular projection $\mu^\perp$ of the candidate $\mu_b^c$ onto the tangent plane of the parent Gaussian.
The tangent plane is defined by point $\mu_a$ and normal $N_V^{(a)}(\bar{x}_a)$.
**Compute Final Position:** Calculate $\mu_c$ using the weighted combination of the candidate and the tangent projection, weighted by the image gradient.
- Image gradient $\nabla I$: Serves as a dynamic weight.
In weakly textured regions (small gradients), the child stays close to the geometric surface ($\mu_c \approx \mu^\perp$).
- **Weakly Textured Regions:** Standard splitting may place splats incorrectly due to lack of visual details.
- **Time Complexity:** Adds overhead for normal map lookup and gradient computation per split operation.
- **Memory Complexity:** Requires storage/access to normal maps and image gradients.
It was developed to address the limitations of standard random splitting in 3D Gaussian Splatting, particularly in areas with low visual detail.
